summary: Frontend-only testing of LendClear DTI Calculator single-page app. Verified header, all 14 input fields with data-testids, P&I amortization formula ($2,270.09 for $350k/6.75%/30yr), income/housing/PITI aggregates, front/back DTI computation (35.12% / 42.11% for the provided scenario), zone labels (Safe/Caution/High Risk), Reset restoring years=30 with other fields empty, and Print button behavior (toast 'Enter monthly income before printing' when income=0; window.print() called when income present). 31/33 checks passed.

ui_bugs.issue: Floating-point precision causes boundary misclassification. At exactly 28% front-end DTI (e.g. income $10,000, property tax $2,800), UI shows 'Caution' instead of 'Safe' because 2800/10000*100 evaluates to 28.000000000000004 in JS, failing the <=28 check. Same risk exists for 35, 36, 43 boundaries though 35% and 36% happened to classify correctly in testing. Recommended fix: round pct to 2 decimals before zone comparison, or use epsilon tolerance (e.g., pct <= 28 + 1e-9).

action_items: Optional: fix floating-point boundary in frontEndZone/backEndZone in /app/frontend/src/lib/dti.js (round percent or add epsilon) so that exactly 28%/36%/43% land in the correct zone.
critical_code_review_comments: dti.js zone functions use raw <= comparisons on floating-point percentages — vulnerable to precision errors at boundaries.
monthlyPI, fmt helpers, and useMemo memoization look clean and correct.
All interactive elements have data-testid attributes as required.
Print gating logic (income <= 0) is implemented correctly and shows a sonner toast.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Frontend fully covered. Only minor floating-point boundary edge in zone classification remains. All specified DTI math, testids, reset, and print behaviors verified against public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL.
rca of the issue: At exactly 28% front-end DTI, JS computation (2800/10000)*100 yields 28.000000000000004 due to IEEE-754 representation of 0.28. frontEndZone uses `pct <= 28` which returns false for 28.000...004, causing the value to fall into the 'warn' (Caution) bucket. Fix: `const p = Math.round(pct * 100) / 100;` before comparisons, or use `pct <= 28 + 1e-9`.
